title: Trellis perf log: burst-echo microbench (scratch)
content:
Goal: quick scratchpad to capture a weird tail pattern observed on the trellis staging pool when small bursts (5-30 reqs over 200ms) arrive with a high fraction of cached prefixes.

Short summary / hypothesis:
- Observed recurring p99 spikes (~2.5-3x baseline) immediately after short bursts; p50/p95 largely unaffected.
- Hypothesis: micro-coalescing backpressure + KV-cache priming causes a transient scheduling stall on the GPU worker that shows up only when request arrival is both bursty and highly prefix-cache-hit (>80%).
- Alternative: cpu-side pre-processing jitter (tokenizer) coupled with a batching threshold race.

Environment / config used for this run:
- Fleet: trellis-staging-a (4x A100-80GB nodes simulated via dev pool)
- Runtime build: serving-runtime@feature/fast-coalesce (commit a1b2c3d)
- Model: redwood-open-v1-medium (quantized 8-bit experimental)
- KV-cache: enabled, in-worker (local), served hits reported by telemetry
- Batching policy: dynamic with target_batch_ms=12, min_batch=1, max_batch_size=64
- Arrival generator: synthetic client (node) — poisson baseline qps=15, superimposed micro-bursts: 5–30 reqs over 150–300ms at 60s intervals
- Concurrency: client-level concurrency 20
- Payload: prompt lengths 40–80 tokens; generation 128 tokens max; average token size ~3.8

Commands (notes):
- load test: ./tools/loadgen --target qps 15 --burst-size 10 --burst-width 0.22 --seed 42 --warmup 30s --run 900s
- server flags: --batch-ms 12 --kv-local=true --prefill=false --metric-exporter=prom

Observations (timestamped):
- 00:00–00:30 warmup: everything stable, p50 ~42ms, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~185ms, token/s per GPU ~6200
- 00:31 burst #1 (size 12, width 0.18s): p99 spikes to 540ms for ~0.6s window, p95 unchanged. KV-hit rate ~86%
- 01:31 burst #2 (size 8, width 0.22s): p99 spikes to 470ms, CPU sys time on worker that served majority of requests jumped +28% relative baseline for the 1s window
- 02:31 burst #3 (size 24): similar spike pattern, but longer tail (~1.2s) and a small drop in throughput (~6%) while batch formation paused

Quick micro-profiling (lightweight):
- sampled stack traces during spike: ~60% time in work queue wakeup path, ~25% time in tokenizer::normalize, ~15% in kernel submission
- heap+locks: a short-lived mutex contention on batch-queue when kv-cache hit-rate > 80% (reproduced with flamegraphs)

Ad-hoc ascii sketch of the event (not precise):
- client burst -> many reqs hit KV -> worker bypasses prefill path -> requests hit fastpath but contend on batch-queue wake -> scheduler does fast coalesce, finds batch too small -> batch timer expires -> kernel submit flood -> submit backpressure + lock contention -> p99 spike

Initial actionable hypotheses to test (ranked):
1) Race between KV-fastpath and batch-queue locking when many requests bypass prefill; adding a per-worker async enqueue (lock-free) should reduce stall.
2) Tokenizer jitter: ensure tokenizer is offloaded or pre-tokenized at client when bursts expected. Run a test with pre-tokenized payloads.
3) Batch timer tuning: increase target_batch_ms to 18–20ms to see whether coalescing reduces number of tiny kernel submissions (cost: +p50).
4) KV-cache eviction/priming effect: artificially lower KV-hit to 40% and re-run to isolate whether hits amplify contention.

Small experiment matrix (planned runs):
- A: baseline (as above) x3 seeds
- B: target_batch_ms=18 x3 seeds
- C: kv-local=false (remote cache rpc) x2 seeds
- D: client pre-tokenize payloads x2 seeds
- E: apply lock-free enqueue patch (dev branch) x1 seed (if patch lands)

Preliminary quick results (first two short runs):
- B (batch_ms=18): p99 spike amplitude dropped by ~35% but p50 increased ~8ms; total tokens/s per GPU ~-4%
- D (pre-tokenize): tokenizer sys time drop as expected; p99 spikes smaller (~20% reduction) but not eliminated

Open questions / oddities to debug:
- Why does contention correlate strongly with high KV-hit? (Expected the opposite)
- Is there a subtle priority inversion when fastpath requests skip prefill and touch the same queue as slowpath?
- Are there scheduler fairness bugs when many small kernel submissions occur in quick succession?

Notes for next run (quick checklist):
- [ ] Increase batch-ms to 18 and schedule 6x longer runs (30m) to check steady-state impact
- [ ] Reproduce with kv-local=false to see if network rpc smooths the spike (i.e., remote cache adds latency but reduces lock contention)
- [ ] Add per-worker ring buffer enqueue patch to dev branch and bench
- [ ] Trace thread-level scheduling during a reproduced spike (finer-grained samples)

Useful links / references:
- PERF-719 ticket (sketch + prometheus charts pinned)
- PR-289 touches coalescing path (note: not yet merged)
- Confluence sketch: Trellis micro-burst hypothesis

Notes to self: keep this as a reproducible lab script. If we can show that small increase in batch-ms reduces tail significantly, that's an easy knob for Dedicated customers as an SLO tuning knob. But need to quantify real cost (per-token).

Random scribbles: trellis->trellis-rungs metaphor helps explain how tiny bursts climb the scheduling rungs and then fall — visualize as ladder of coalescing windows. Might reuse in doc or deck.
